title: Human Digestion: Terms, Processes & Enzymes
topic: Digestive Tract Organs, Enzymes, and Conditions
subject: Science

questions.question: What physical property must large, complex food substances acquire through digestion before they can pass through the walls of the digestive tract into the bloodstream?
options: They must be converted into solid crystals.
They must become small and soluble.
They must be large and insoluble.
questions.explanation: Food substances must be broken down into small and soluble molecules so they can dissolve and easily absorb through the living membranes of the digestive walls.

questions.question: Which of the following processes is classified as physical digestion?
options: Enzymes breaking down starch molecules in the mouth.
Teeth grinding and chewing large food chunks into smaller pieces.
Enzymes breaking down protein chains inside the stomach.
Enzymes converting oil droplets into fatty acids and glycerol.
questions.explanation: Chewing and grinding with teeth reduces the physical size of food particles to increase their surface area, without changing the chemical nature of the molecules.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes what happens during chemical digestion?
options: Food is moved through the esophagus by wave-like muscle actions.
Water is absorbed from undigested waste matter in the large intestine.
Large, complex food molecules are broken down into new, simpler substances by enzymes.
Food is cut and crushed mechanically into smaller fragments by the teeth.
questions.explanation: Chemical digestion involves a chemical change where large, complex food molecules are broken down into entirely new, simpler, and soluble molecules with the help of enzymes.

questions.question: A student eats a meal containing a high amount of rice, bread, and potatoes. Which primary class of nutrients do these foods provide?
questions.explanation: Starchy foods like rice, bread, and potatoes are excellent sources of carbohydrates, which provide the body with its primary source of energy.

questions.question: Why does a growing teenager require a sufficient daily intake of foods like chicken breast, fish, eggs, and tofu?
options: They provide the quickest source of instant energy for daily running.
They turn directly into a thick layer of fat to insulate internal organs.
They dissolve essential vitamins so they can be exhaled easily.
They provide proteins necessary for cell growth and tissue repair.
questions.explanation: Chicken, fish, eggs, and tofu are rich in proteins, which supply the essential materials needed to build new cells and repair worn-out tissues.

questions.question: During chemical digestion, protease enzymes break down complex protein chains into which final, soluble end-products?
questions.explanation: When proteases fully digest protein molecules, the chemical chains are completely broken apart into individual, small, and soluble units called amino acids.

questions.question: What are the final, soluble end-products produced when lipase enzymes fully digest a lipid (fat) molecule?
questions.explanation: The chemical digestion of a lipid molecule yields two distinct types of smaller, soluble end-products: fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.question: What is the final, soluble simple sugar produced from the full digestion of complex carbohydrates that is directly absorbed into the blood?
questions.explanation: Large carbohydrates (like starch) are chemically digested by carbohydrases down into their smallest, simplest unit, which is glucose.

questions.question: Which enzyme is produced by the salivary glands in the mouth to begin the chemical breakdown of starch?
questions.explanation: Chemical digestion of carbohydrates starts in the mouth, where salivary amylase begins breaking down complex starch into maltose.

questions.question: What is the role of the esophagus in the digestive system?
options: To transport food from the mouth to the stomach
questions.explanation: The esophagus is a muscular tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.

questions.question: What kind of environment do protease enzymes in the stomach require to function at their best?
options: A strongly acidic environment provided by hydrochloric acid
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid inside gastric juice creates a strongly acidic environment, which is the optimal pH level required for stomach proteases to work.

questions.question: In which organ does the final completion of chemical digestion and the bulk absorption of nutrients into the bloodstream take place?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is highly adapted to complete the chemical breakdown of all nutrient classes and absorb the resulting soluble molecules into the blood.

questions.question: How do the millions of microscopic, finger-like projections (villi) on the inner walls of the small intestine assist in nutrition?
options: They increase the internal surface area for the absorption of nutrients.
They churn and mix food mechanically to assist physical digestion.
They secrete strong hydrochloric acid to kill harmful bacteria.
They act as temporary pouches to store undigested solid feces.
questions.explanation: Villi vastly increase the internal surface area of the small intestine, allowing soluble nutrients to be absorbed into the bloodstream much faster.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the large intestine when handling undigested food matter?
options: To digest remaining proteins into soluble amino acids
To absorb water and mineral salts from the undigested food material
To secrete lipase enzymes for the final chemical breakdown of fats
To produce bile to break down remaining fat droplets
questions.explanation: The large intestine does not digest food chemically. Instead, it reabsorbs water and mineral salts from the undigested waste material, turning it into solid feces.

questions.question: What is the role of the rectum in the digestive system?
questions.explanation: The rectum is the final section of the large intestine where solid feces are stored temporarily before being passed out.

questions.question: What is the main function of the anus?
options: To control the release of feces from the body
questions.explanation: The anus is a ring of muscle (sphincter) that controls the elimination of feces from the body.

questions.question: Which organ functions as an accessory gland that delivers a juice containing carbohydrase, protease, and lipase enzymes into the small intestine?
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice, which contains a complete mix of enzymes designed to chemically break down carbohydrates, proteins, and fats inside the small intestine.

questions.question: Why is dietary fibre highly important for human digestive health, even though our body cells cannot digest or absorb it?
options: It provides the brain with an immediate source of glucose energy.
It adds bulk to food matter to stimulate peristalsis and prevent constipation.
It is neutralized by stomach acid to form essential mineral salts.
It is converted into proteins by helpful bacteria in the esophagus.
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre adds bulk to undigested materials, which stimulates the muscular walls of the intestines to contract, moving waste smoothly and preventing constipation.

questions.question: Type 2 Diabetes develops when the body cells fail to respond properly to which critical pancreatic hormone?
questions.explanation: Insulin is the hormone responsible for signaling body cells to absorb glucose from the blood. In Type 2 Diabetes, cells become resistant to insulin, causing blood sugar levels to rise dangerously.

questions.question: A person has their gallbladder removed. Why might their doctor recommend eating smaller, lower-fat meals?
options: Because they can no longer produce bile at all
Because without the gallbladder, bile is released continuously in small amounts, making large fatty meals harder to digest
Because fats are no longer useful to the body
Because fat digestion now happens in the stomach instead
questions.explanation: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile. Without it, bile is released continuously but in smaller amounts, making it difficult to digest large amounts of fat at one time.

questions.question: How does the stomach protect its own lining from being damaged by acid?
options: By producing a thick layer of mucus
By staying empty at all times
By absorbing the acid into the blood
By producing enzymes that destroy acid
questions.explanation: The stomach secretes a layer of mucus that protects its lining from the acidic gastric juices.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the function of the pancreas in digestion?
options: It produces bile to emulsify fats
It produces digestive enzymes and releases them into the small intestine
It absorbs water from waste material
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces a range of digestive enzymes (for carbohydrates, proteins, and fats) and secretes them into the small intestine to complete chemical digestion.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symptom of uncontrolled diabetes?
options: A constant need to eat more fiber
questions.explanation: High blood sugar levels cause the kidneys to work harder to remove excess glucose, leading to frequent urination and increased thirst.

questions.question: Why do we chew our food before swallowing?
options: To increase the surface area of food for enzymes to work on
To turn food into liquid immediately
questions.explanation: Chewing breaks food into smaller pieces, increasing the surface area so digestive enzymes can work more efficiently.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an application of understanding the digestive system?
options: Knowing that eating fiber prevents constipation
Knowing the chemical formula for glucose
Knowing the number of bones in the body
Knowing the boiling point of water
questions.explanation: Understanding that fiber helps prevent constipation is a practical application of digestive system knowledge.

questions.question: What is the main function of the mouth in digestion?
options: To physically break down food and mix it with saliva
To absorb nutrients into the bloodstream
questions.explanation: The mouth physically breaks down food by chewing and mixes it with saliva to begin the digestive process.

questions.question: A student has a diet low in fiber and often feels bloated and uncomfortable. Which condition is she most likely experiencing?
questions.explanation: A low-fiber diet often leads to constipation, which can cause bloating and discomfort.

questions.question: What is the main reason that the small intestine has a very large internal surface area?
options: To allow more food to be stored
To increase the rate of absorption of nutrients
To slow down the movement of food
questions.explanation: The large surface area (created by villi and microvilli) maximizes the absorption of nutrients into the bloodstream.
